what: block_header_crc of TrueHD protected blocks (error_protect). No public document defines the field. The rule checked here: CRC-8, polynomial 0x1D, register from 0xA2, bits most significant first, shift then XOR the bit in, over the bits of the block header alone (after the block-header and restart-header flags and after the restart header, up to block_data_bits); 0xA2 for a block without a header. This file records what was measured of it on Dolby's decoder as a black box; it says nothing of where the rule came from
method: streams written by oadec-synth (recipes and probes named below), wrapped in MP4 with ffmpeg -c:a copy -strict -2 and decoded by the dlbtruehddec element of the Dolby Reference Player as a black box, beside FFmpeg and truehdd (tools/synth_accept.py); check bytes recomputed independently by tools/crc8_reference.py --spans over oadec-synth spans; single faults put in with every other check of the stream (restart header CRC, segment parity and CRC) written again

versions.ffmpeg: ffmpeg version 2026-11-19-git-01ca75d350-full_build-www.gyan.dev Copyright (c) 2000-2026 the FFmpeg developers
versions.dolby: the dlbtruehddec and dlbac3dec elements of the Dolby Reference Player

independent_reference: tools/crc8_reference.py --spans: 48 of 48 check bytes of protected-checked are the CRC of their block header; 8 blocks without a header, 38 headers starting inside a byte, header lengths 16, 24, 27, 35 and 36 bits

single_fault_notes.one_check_byte_struck_header_block: unit 9, a block with a header: Dolby's output is the samples up to unit 8, 40 samples short, other samples up to the next restart header and the samples again after it
single_fault_notes.one_check_byte_struck_headerless_block: the same for a block without a header: the check of a block without a header is checked too, against 0xA2
single_fault_notes.restart_header_bit_resealed: a bit of dither_seed of the first restart header, its CRC written again: Dolby gives the samples, so the restart header is not under block_header_crc
single_fault_notes.data_bits_bit: the lowest bit of block_data_bits of the first block: block.data_bits alone
single_fault_notes.header_bit_resealed: a bit of the first block header flipped in the bytes: the header no longer parses (segment.syntax); probe-protected-header-struck is the isolated form of this fault

findings: Dolby's decoder accepts protected-checked, written with the rule, and gives its samples bit for bit (as FFmpeg and truehdd do)

Dolby's decoder refuses probe-protected-header-struck (every check byte made over a header with one bit the other way, every other check right) and probe-protected (check bytes nought), and gives other samples when the check byte of a single block is wrong: a failing block_header_crc loses audio, so block.header_crc is an error

Dolby's decoder refuses probe-protected-checked-counting-itself, whose check bytes follow the rule and whose block_data_bits count their own 16 bits: it accepts block_data_bits that count the block data alone and not ones that count the field too
